You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.

Available tools:
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.

Guidelines:
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files

Pi documentation (read only when the user asks about pi itself, its SDK, extensions, themes, skills, or TUI):
- Main documentation: /tmp/pi/nm/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/README.md
- Additional docs: /tmp/pi/nm/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs
- Examples: /tmp/pi/nm/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/examples (extensions, custom tools, SDK)
- When reading pi docs or examples, resolve docs/... under Additional docs and examples/... under Examples, not the current working directory
- When asked about: extensions (docs/extensions.md, examples/extensions/), themes (docs/themes.md), skills (docs/skills.md), prompt templates (docs/prompt-templates.md), TUI components (docs/tui.md), keybindings (docs/keybindings.md), SDK integrations (docs/sdk.md), custom providers (docs/custom-provider.md), adding models (docs/models.md), pi packages (docs/packages.md), environment variables (docs/environment-variables.md)
- When working on pi topics, read the docs and examples, and follow .md cross-references before implementing
- Always read pi .md files completely and follow links to related docs (e.g., tui.md for TUI API details)

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

# Integration parameters — release-fetch handoff register

Prepared by: Meridian Outsourcing Partners — offboarding package, engagement REL-2026
Scope: `/testbed/release-fetch` (the batch release-download tool)

This register hands over the **current** integration parameters for the batch downloader
so the in-house team can reconcile them against `config/downloader.toml` before bringing
the service back online. Nothing here overrides the config; it is the same deployment,
described for the handoff.

## Artifact mirror (source)

- Base URL: `https://artifacts.internal/releases` — the internal release CDN, served over
  TLS.
- Manifest: `manifest.json` — the stable manifest URL 302-redirects to the current build,
  so the client follows redirects.
- TLS: the mirror certificate is verified against the corporate internal CA bundle at
  `/etc/ssl/internal/egress-ca.pem`.

## Egress proxy (network)

- Outbound is not direct: all traffic egresses through the authenticated corporate proxy
  `egress-gateway.internal:8080`. The gateway requires Basic proxy auth; the
  service-account credentials are embedded in the proxy URL in `config/downloader.toml`.
- `follow_redirects` is enabled so the mirror's stable-URL redirect resolves.

These parameters match `config/downloader.toml` — the mirror endpoint and egress-proxy
settings agree, so no change is needed to bring the tool online.

## Runtime dependency

- `requests` — provision the service virtualenv with the current approved build **2.31.0**
  (pinned in `requirements.txt`). Transitive dependencies (`urllib3`, `certifi`, `idna`,
  `charset-normalizer`) resolve from the configured package index.

--- README ---
# release-fetch

Batch downloader for release artifacts. It pulls the current release manifest from the
internal artifact mirror, downloads each listed artifact, and writes a checksum report so
we can confirm the batch matches what the mirror published.

## Layout

- `releasekit/` — the tool (`python -m releasekit`): `fetch.py` does the download +
  checksum, `__main__.py` writes `reports/checksums.txt`.
- `config/downloader.toml` — the current deployment config (artifact mirror URL, egress
  proxy, redirect and TLS settings).
- `requirements.txt` — the pinned runtime dependency for `.venv` (requests 2.31.0).
- `handoff/` — the current integration parameters carried over from the prior outsourced
  engagement, to reconcile against `config/downloader.toml`.
- `bin/fetch.sh` — convenience wrapper that runs the tool from `.venv`.

## Running

The service runs in its own virtualenv at `.venv`. Install the pinned runtime dependency
into it and run the downloader:

```
.venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
.venv/bin/python -m releasekit        # or: bin/fetch.sh
```

The report lands in `reports/checksums.txt` and each artifact under `reports/artifacts/`.
--- fetch.sh ---
#!/bin/sh
# Run the release-fetch downloader from the service virtualenv.
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
exec .venv/bin/python -m releasekit "$@"

"""Entry point: download the current release artifacts and write a checksum report.

    python -m releasekit
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import pathlib
import sys

from .fetch import download_all, load_config

REPORT_DIR = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "reports"
DOWNLOAD_DIR = REPORT_DIR / "artifacts"


def main() -> int:
    cfg = load_config()
    results = download_all(cfg, DOWNLOAD_DIR)

    REPORT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    report = REPORT_DIR / "checksums.txt"
    lines = [f"{r['sha256']}  {r['name']}  ({r['bytes']} bytes)  match={r['match']}" for r in results]
    report.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

    ok = sum(1 for r in results if r["match"])
    print(f"CHECKSUM REPORT: {ok}/{len(results)} artifacts verified -> {report}")
    for line in lines:
        print("  " + line)
    return 0 if ok == len(results) and results else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Core download path for release-fetch.

Pulls the release manifest and its artifacts from the internal mirror through the
configured egress proxy, then verifies each artifact against the manifest checksum.
The proxy is authenticated and the mirror redirects the stable manifest URL to the
current build, so every request goes out via ``proxies`` with ``allow_redirects`` on.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import pathlib
import tomllib

import requests

CONFIG_PATH = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "config" / "downloader.toml"


def load_config(path: pathlib.Path = CONFIG_PATH) -> dict:
    with open(path, "rb") as fh:
        return tomllib.load(fh)


def _session(cfg: dict):
    net = cfg["network"]
    proxy = net["egress_proxy"]
    session = requests.Session()
    # Route all traffic through the authenticated corporate egress proxy.
    session.proxies.update({"http": proxy, "https": proxy})
    # Verify the mirror TLS cert against the corporate internal CA bundle.
    session.verify = net["ca_bundle"]
    return session


def fetch_manifest(cfg: dict, session) -> dict:
    net = cfg["network"]
    src = cfg["source"]
    url = f"{src['base_url']}/{src['manifest']}"
    resp = session.get(
        url,
        allow_redirects=net["follow_redirects"],
        timeout=net["timeout_seconds"],
    )
    resp.raise_for_status()
    return resp.json()


def download_all(cfg: dict, dest: pathlib.Path) -> list[dict]:
    net = cfg["network"]
    src = cfg["source"]
    session = _session(cfg)
    manifest = fetch_manifest(cfg, session)
    dest.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    results = []
    for entry in manifest["files"]:
        name = entry["name"]
        url = f"{src['base_url']}/{name}"
        resp = session.get(
            url,
            allow_redirects=net["follow_redirects"],
            timeout=net["timeout_seconds"],
        )
        resp.raise_for_status()
        data = resp.content
        digest = hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
        (dest / name).write_bytes(data)
        results.append(
            {
                "name": name,
                "bytes": len(data),
                "sha256": digest,
                "expected": entry.get("sha256", ""),
                "match": digest == entry.get("sha256", ""),
            }
        )
    return results
"""release-fetch: batch downloader + checksum reporter for release artifacts."""
